{{Quote|The ash of the Taung beats strong within the Mandalorians' heart!|Excerpt from the traditional ''[[Dha Werda Verda]]'' chant|<ref name="TBHC">''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''</ref>}}
The '''Taungs''' were an ancient [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Primate/Legends|simians]]. [[Homeworld/Legends|Indigenous]] to the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the two-[[Meter/Legends|meter]]-tall, [[Color/Legends|gray]]-skinned Taungs were [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]] from [[Youngling/Legends|youth]], and viewed battle as a source of honor both for the individual and their [[God/Legends|gods]]. Famous for their struggles against the [[Battalion/Legends|Battalions]] of [[Zhell/Legends|Zhell]]—prehistoric Coruscant's other species —the Taungs waged war against their enemies for hundreds of [[Standard year/Legends|years]]. When a powerful [[Volcano/Legends|volcano]] erupted and devastated the Zhell, spewing ash into the [[Atmosphere/Legends|sky]] with such density it blocked out the light of Coruscant's [[Coruscant Prime/Legends|sun]], the Taungs labeled themselves the "'''Warriors of the Shadow'''", or '''''Dha Werda Verda''''' in [[Mando'a/Legends|their language]]. Despite their loss, the Zhell eventually managed to drive the Taungs from Coruscant, and the defeated Taungs fled to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Roon/Legends|Roon]], located in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]. There they remained for millennia, until legendary [[Mandalore the First]] led the Taungs to conquer a new world which they named [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] in honor of their [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|leader]], and the Taungs subsequently recast themselves as the '''Mandalorians''' or '''''Mando'ade'''''—"Sons and Daughters of Mandalore."

As the newly entitled [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]], the Taungs set out to conquer the worlds around their new home, their nomadic nature and worship of war driving them crusading outward as they increased [[Mandalore sector/Legends|their territory]]. Under the rule of [[Mandalore the Indomitable]], another Taung warlord following in the leadership tradition established by Mandalore the First, the Taungs began to take in beings of other species into their culture, transforming what it meant to be Mandalorian forever after. This willing acceptance of other beings peaked during the [[Mandalorian Wars]], when [[Mandalore the Ultimate]] led the Mandalorians on a campaign against the [[Army/Legends|military]] [[Republic Military/Legends|forces]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Though initially victorious, the intervention of the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] and his loyal [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Revanchist|followers]] turned the tide of the war against the Mandalorians, culminating with the [[Battle of Malachor V|devastation]] of the planet [[Malachor V]]. The Taung race had suffered heavy losses during the war, and by its end, were generally believed to have drifted into extinction, survived by the legacy of the Mandalorian culture they had passed on, which remembered the Taungs as the '''Progenitors'''.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|We call the Shadow Warriors our Progenitors, though we do not share their blood, and their bodies were those of beasts, not humans.|[[Tor Vizsla]]|<ref name="TBHC" />}}
A [[Humanoid/Legends|Humanoid]] [[Species/Legends|species]], the Taungs were a [[Foot/Legends|bipedal]]<ref name="GaW" /> race of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Primate/Legends|simians]]. [[Color/Legends|Gray]]-skinned<ref name="HotM" /> and [[Color/Legends|yellow]]-[[Eye/Legends|eyed]], Taungs were typically tall and strong. On average, Taungs reached a height of two [[Meter/Legends|meters]], and weighed around ninety-five [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]]. Taungs were known to be extremely resilient, able to endure physical hardships that many other species could not. Their five fingers were tipped with sharp claws, and bony ridges adorned the top of their [[Skeleton/Legends|skulls]]. Taung lifespans were known to reach and occasionally exceed eighty-five [[Standard year/Legends|years]]. Considered children until the age of six, Taungs attained adulthood when they turned thirteen, passed through middle age between the years of forty-six and sixty-four, and were viewed as elderly beyond the age of sixty-five. Galactic historical records document no known instances of Taungs with a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|sensitivity]] to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="GaW" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Soon, rumors reached the Republic of worlds ruled by ferocious warriors. They served the god Kad Ha'rangir, whose tests and trials forced change and growth upon the clans he chose to be his people.|[[Historian/Legends|Historian]] [[Vilnau Teupt]]|<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Taung.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Taung armored helmets resembled their facial structure]]
Taung society was nomadic and clan-based. Veterans of successful campaigns were honored, and looked upon with reverence. These battle-tested elders became [[Chief/Legends|chieftains]], ''de facto'' leaders of their clan and community; higher authority came only from the<ref name="GaW" /> [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']], a title that meant "Sole Ruler" in the Taung [[Language/Legends|language]],<ref name="TMPaC" /> and a role that embodied a single leader of all the [[Soldier/Legends|warrior]] clans.<ref name="HotM" /> These aspects continued on throughout later [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] culture long after the Taungs themselves had passed from the galaxy.<ref name="TMPaC" /> Pragmatism and ruthlessness were common traits among the Taungs, matched only by their loyalty to their clan kinsmen. Their practical nature was reflected in their naming practices, typically choosing names that corresponded to traits they deemed desirable. Common names included such examples as Atin, Kot, and Tor—meaning "persistent", "strength", and "justice", respectively.<ref name="GaW" /> The Taungs spoke an archaic form<ref name="TMPaC" /> of what later became the Mandalorian language of [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']].<ref name="GaW" />

The civilization of the Taungs was one steeped in war, and the Taungs were warriors above all else. Their combat-centered nature<ref name="GaW" /> gave rise to a religious warrior society governed by elaborate laws that evolved into the [[Canons of Honor]]. Early in their history, the Taungs waged war as a means of ritual worship to their [[God/Legends|god]]<ref name="HotM" /> [[Kad Ha'rangir]]—a destroyer god they believed to personify change and growth. The Taungs sought the favor of Kad Ha'rangir as they denied the temptations of [[Arasuum]], the sloth-god who was an avatar of idleness and stagnation.<ref name="EGW" /> But after the Taungs had recast themselves as the Mandalorians,<ref name="HotM" /> and [[Mandalore the Indomitable]] had risen to lead them, the act of war itself became the center of Mandalorian worship, and to wage war was to ''be'' divine.<ref name="EGW" /> Disputes were resolved through Taung [[Blood/Legends|blood]] duels that involved a challenge to single combat in a fight to the [[Death/Legends|death]].<ref name="Honor">{{TORcite|type=faction|Imperial|Honor Regained|Nar Shaddaa}}</ref>

Despite their violent, warring nature, the Taungs were far from primitive, and maintained a high priority of procuring the latest in technological advancement whenever possible, often through the plundering of a defeated foe. The tradition of [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|Mandalorian armor]] began with the culture's Taung founders,<ref name="HotM" /> and their unique [[Armor/Legends|helmets]] and war masks were forged in the image of the Taungs' face, including slanted outer angles and a pointed chin.<ref name="GaW" /> Unlike later iterations, the armor of the Taungs was sparse in its armament due to their belief that it was [[Unarmed combat/Legends|unarmed combat]] that brought the highest honor.<ref name="HotM" /> Taung children were trained in martial arts from a young age, and tested themselves repeatedly in numerous physical and mental challenges prior to achieving adulthood. The experience and skills they obtained through their robust upbringing made wandering Taungs valuable assets to [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] companies.<ref name="GaW" />

==History==
===War for a world===
[[File:Last_Stand_of_the_Taungs.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The last stand of the Taungs]]
{{Quote|When the dawn came the Zhell awakened and saw the Taungs upon the high place and were afraid, for the morning light caught the glint of helms and weapons and created phantom warriors, made of dazzle and distance. But the cleverest of them were not deceived, and saw how few we were. And so they assembled without haste, merry in mockery, and prepared to march. And in the high place we awaited death.|Basic-translated excerpt from the ninth chapter of the Dha Werda Verda|<ref name="EGW" />}}
The Taungs evolved on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]],<ref name="GaW" /> located in the central region of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] known as the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]. During the [[pre-Republic era]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> the Taungs inhabited Coruscant alongside the other major power to arise on the prehistoric world, the [[Zhell/Legends|Zhell]]. The Zhell—thirteen tribes of [[Human/Legends|Humans]] who also evolved on ancient Coruscant<ref name="TCSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>—and the Taungs waged war against each other for hundreds of [[Standard year/Legends|years]], struggling for control of the planet.<ref name="GaW" /> At some point amidst their warring, a [[Volcano/Legends|volcanic]] eruption brought devastation upon the [[Battalion/Legends|Battalions]] of Zhell, when it smothered their [[City/Legends|city]] with thick ash and nearly [[Speciecide|destroyed]] the early Human race. The enormous plume of released ash and smoke was so dense and wide-spread across the [[Atmosphere/Legends|sky]], that it blocked out the light from Coruscant's [[Coruscant Prime/Legends|sun]], leaving the land beneath in darkness for two years. The Taungs leaped at the advantage nature had provided, and in the aftermath of the eruption, subjugated their age-old enemy. They viewed the smoke and shadow as an emblem of their destiny, and it was then that they adopted the name ''[[Dha Werda Verda]]'' for themselves, a title that meant "Warriors of the Shadow" in the Taung language.<ref name="TCSWE" />

However, the Taungs' victory over the Zhell was doomed to be a fleeting one. Over [[Time/Legends|time]], the Zhell eventually managed to win back control of Coruscant<ref name="TCSWE" /> and drive the Taungs from their shared homeworld.<ref name="GaW" /> Though an offshoot sect of [[Priest/Legends|priestly]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] Taungs fled Coruscant for the galaxy's [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] in pursuit of atonement through introspective meditation,<ref name="TUR">''[[The Unknown Regions]]''</ref> the majority of the Taungs were forced to flee to the planet [[Roon/Legends|Roon]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]], there the Taungs remained until the legendary leader, [[Mandalore the First]], led his people to seek a new world.<ref name="GaW" /> The Taungs found another planet in the Outer Rim—a world of multiple ecosystems, uninhabited by intelligent life, and dominated only by a race of non-sentient creatures of colossal size known as [[Mythosaur/Legends|mythosaurs]]—and claimed this new planet as their own.<ref name="TEA" />

===Mandalorian rebirth===
{{Main|Mandalorian/Legends}}
[[File:Mandalorian_on_dxun.jpg|thumb|left|180px|The future [[Mandalore the Ultimate]] looks for [[Mandalore the Indomitable]].]]
{{Quote|We are the rage of the Warriors of the Shadow! The first noble sons of Mandalore!|Excerpt from the traditional ''Dha Werda Verda'' chant|<ref name="TBHC" />}}
In honor of their leader, Mandalore the First, the Taungs named the newly conquered world [[Mandalore/Legends|''Manda'yaim'']],<ref name="TEA" /> or "home of the ''Mand'alor'',<ref name="Mando'a">{{WebCite|url=http://www.karentraviss.com/page20/page26/index.html|text=Mando'a|author=Karen Traviss|work=[http://www.karentraviss.com Karen Traviss]|archivedate=20110925083955}}</ref> which was later transliterated simply as Mandalore in the language of [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]]. Similarly, the Taungs recast themselves as the Mandalorians,<ref name="GaW" /> or ''Mando'ade'': "sons and daughters of Mandalore."<ref name="TZ">''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]''</ref> The newly branded Mandalorians set to taming their new world, and in the process slaughtered the enormous mythosaurs, leaving only their skeletons behind.<ref name="TEA" /> The planet Mandalore became the home of fierce clans of masked Taung warriors led by a single warlord who always adopted the name ''Mand'alor'',<ref name="TCSWE" /> meaning "sole ruler" in their language,<ref name="Mando'a" /> after Mandalore the First.<ref name="TCSWE" /> Over time, however, a single world proved not to be enough for the Mandalorian Taungs, and they set out to conquer other planets and battle new foes.<ref name="TEA" />

The Mandalorians warred with the [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] [[Nevoota/Legends|Nevoota]] species, a [[Nevoota Extinction|conflict]] which saw the demise of the Nevoota and the deification of war itself by the early Mandalorians. With this new religious shift, the Taungs' conquests evolved into holy crusades, and they took on the additional, informal descriptor of "[[Mandalorian Crusaders]]." Their new outlook led the Crusaders to later annihilate several other species in their entirety, including the [[Fenelar]], [[Kuaran]]s, [[Tlönian]]s, and the [[Basiliskan]]s—obtaining their infamous [[Basilisk war droid/Legends|Basilisk war droid]] mounts from the latter. The Taungs only truly met their match with the inhabitants of the planet neighboring their new homeworld of Mandalore, [[Mandallia]]. The native [[Mandallian Giant]]s were large in stature and ferocious in combat, repelling the Taungs' offensive in such a manner that the Mandallians earned the respect of their would-be conquerors, and were granted the opportunity to fight beside them as fellow Mandalorians. Yet the Mandallians were only the first non-Taungs taken into the Mandalorian fold, and as the Mandalorians continued to strike at other worlds,<ref name="HotM" /> individuals that impressed the warriors were often accepted into the culture,<ref name="TMPaC" /> including the likes of the [[Zeltron/Legends|Zeltron]] [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] [[Demagol|Antos Wyrick]] and numerous other [[Iskalloni]] [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]], who joined after the Crusaders' [[Raid on Iskadrell|invasion]] of [[Iskadrell]].<ref name="Demon">[[Knights of the Old Republic 48|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 48]]</ref> This willing acceptance of beings from other species forever changed what it meant to be a Mandalorian, moving the word from simply another name for the Taungs,<ref name="HotM" /> to an encompassing term for a single shared culture uniting many different beings.<ref name="TMPaC" />

===Old Sith Wars and decline===
{{Quote|It's my belief that 'Rage of the Shadow Warriors' dates from the reign of Mandalore the Ultimate, when the Taungs knew they were being eclipsed. I've always thought it a poignant work—a plea that the Taungs not be forgotten by the newborn culture they knew would outlive them.|[[Hu Jibwe]], military historian|<ref name="EGTW Author's Cut">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-2-ancient-coruscant|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 2 - Ancient Coruscant}}</ref>}}
The Mandalorians, both Taungs and otherwise, were drawn into the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]] when the latest in the tradition of the ''Mand'alor'', a Taung warrior by the sobriquet [[Mandalore the Indomitable]], challenged the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends|Ulic Qel-Droma]]. The former [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Duel on Kuar|bested]] Mandalore the Indomitable in [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|single combat]] on the planet [[Kuar]], and from that point the ''Mand'alor'' swore the loyalty of he and his followers to Qel-Droma and, by extension, his [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Master]] [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]].<ref name="TSW1">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 1|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 1]]</ref> The Mandalorians waged war against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] on behalf of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], even striking against their former homeworld of Coruscant, but when they had been tasked with taking the planet [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]] late in the campaign, Mandalore the Indomitable was slain within the [[Tree/Legends|jungles]] of Onderon's [[Moon/Legends|moon]], [[Dxun/Legends|Dxun]]. Another Taung took up his ceremonial [[Mandalore's Mask|mask]] and became the new ''Mand'alor'',<ref name="TSW6">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 6|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 6]]</ref> proclaiming himself [[Mandalore the Ultimate]]. The new ''Mand'alor''—spurred on by elements of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] in hiding<ref name="Revan">''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]''</ref>—encouraged the Taung belief that the foretold "Last Great Battle" was fast approaching. Under his leadership, the acceptance of non-Taungs into the Mandalorian culture grew to an all-time high as he prepared for full-scale war against the Galactic Republic.<ref name="HotM" />

[[File:Mandalorians_-_TEA.jpg|thumb|right|280px|[[Mandalore the Indomitable]] leads his Taung warriors into battle atop [[Basilisk war droid/Legends|Basilisk war droids]].]]
Under Mandalore the Ultimate, the Mandalorians expanded [[Mandalore sector/Legends|their sector]] of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] as they proceeded to conquer world after world until the Republic finally moved to engage the rising Mandalorian threat. In what became known as the [[Mandalorian Wars]],<ref name="TEA" /> one of several conflicts that were later grouped under the unofficial compilation, the "[[Old Sith Wars]],"<ref name="HotM" /> the Republic clashed with [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders]] across the galaxy in a sixteen-year-long struggle. However, it was only with the intervention of a [[Revanchist|group]] of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] lead by the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Revan/Legends|Revan]], that the Republic was truly able to turn the tide against the Mandalorians.<ref name="TEA" /> Revan [[Battle of Malachor V|fought]] and killed Mandalore the Ultimate at [[Malachor V]], bringing an end to the Mandalorian Wars not long after.<ref name="Revan" />

The Mandalorian Wars had been one of the bloodiest conflicts in the history of the Republic,<ref name="Timeline9">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 9: The Mandalorian Wars|int=Timeline 9: The Mandalorian Wars}}</ref> and the casualties among the Taung species had been severe. By the war's end, most believed that the Taungs had been driven to extinction,<ref name="HotM" /> though at least one Mandalorian Taung—an unsubstantiated [[Unidentified Mandalore|claimant]] to the title of ''Mand'alor''—survived for several years after the war's end.<ref name="KotORCG">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Several hundred years later, during the time of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]]—a proxy conflict between the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] and Galactic Republic—a number of surviving female Taungs from the priestly [[Warriors of Shadow]] sect [[Battle above a nameless moon|fought]] the religious order of the [[Knell of Muspilli]] above a [[Unidentified moon (Unknown Regions)|nameless moon]] in the Unknown Regions. Eventually, someone was sent to study the wreckage of the battle that had been left behind.<ref name="ARCH">{{TORcite|type=crewskill|Archaelogy|Battle of Terror}}</ref>

===Legacy===
{{Quote|Leeber soong whar tung tach picta / Manner manner migta richta / Schelecht varn toom-soing pa ho-grunten / Gersh ve dala funken mimpa / Droit! / To Gropen wettkampf Zunken!|[[Notron Cant|Ancient Basic]] excerpt from the ''Dha Werda Verda'' poem left behind on [[Roon/Legends|Roon]]|<ref name="SotE">[[Shadows of the Empire (soundtrack)|''Shadows of the Empire'' soundtrack]] liner notes</ref>}}
[[File:Mandalorian_wedding.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The Mandalorian culture came to embrace beings from all species, including numerous Humans.]]
Long after the Taungs' departure from the galaxy, their impact remained.<ref name="HotM" /> In [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]],<ref name="Polyhedron170">{{PolyhedronCite|170|Star Wars Droids: The Adventures of R2-D2 and C-3PO}}</ref> the Human [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]] [[Mungo Baobab]] discovered the fabled [[Roonstone]]s on the planet Roon.<ref name="Droids">''[[Star Wars: Droids: The Adventures of R2-D2 and C-3PO]]''</ref> Encoded in one of the Roonstones was an ancient recording of the poem ''Dha Werda Verda'', detailing the Taungs' struggle against the Zhell on prehistoric Coruscant in an [[Notron Cant|archaic form]] of Basic.<ref name="SotE" /> Another iteration of the ''Dha Werda Verda'', a thunderous battle chant in ''Mando'a'', was passed through Mandalorian culture for ages, and even adapted by ''Mand'alor'' [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] for [[Clone cadet/Legends|clone trainees]] in the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] prior to the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="TZ" /> The [[Taung Heights]], a region of the [[Galactic City/Legends|Galactic City]] on Coruscant, shared its name with the species.<ref name="HNN 45">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|45|news/13228_2.html|Mass Aqualish Exodus Expected}}</ref>

The Taungs' most lasting contribution to the history of the galaxy was the Mandalorian culture itself, which outlived its founders by more than four thousand years.<ref>''[[Chronicles of the Old Republic]]'' lists the end of the Mandalorian Wars—the relative point of Taung extinction put forward by [[The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors|''The History of the Mandalorians'']]—as [[3960 BBY]]. The latest chronological appearance of the Mandalorians is [[Legacy (2006) 41|''Legacy'' (2006) 41]], which takes place in [[137 ABY]].</ref> Though [[Sentientologist|anthropologists]] would later be divided over whether it was indeed the Taungs who were the first Mandalorians,<ref name="TMPaC" /> quarreling over the similarities between the Mandalorian language and the remaining Taung texts,<ref name="HotM" /> the Mandalorians followed in the example of the Taungs<ref name="GaW" /> as nomadic warriors for much of their history, though they became a much more diversified group of beings from countless species and walks of life, all united by the common culture.<ref name="TMPaC" />

Far from the warrior culture of the Mandalorians, the [[Warriors of Shadow]]―the sisterhood of priestly Taungs that elected to flee ancient Coruscant for the Unknown Regions after their defeat at the [[Limb/Legends|hands]] of the Zhell―had a profound impact on the foundation of an entirely different group altogether: the [[Sorcerers of Rhand]]. These female Taungs, who believed in seeking atonement through meditation and introspection, joined the Knell of Muspilli death cult, and the fanatical [[Kanzer Exiles]] to inspire the teachings of the Sorcerers of [[Rhand]], when over thousands of years, the three unique philosophies and belief systems merged to form a unique new culture that revered the [[Way of the Dark]].<ref name="TUR" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Taung were first mentioned in the liner notes for the [[Shadows of the Empire (soundtrack)|''Shadows of the Empire'' soundtrack]].<ref name="SotE" /> The ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' article, "[[The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors|The History of the Mandalorians]]" [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]]<ref name="HotM" /> the Mandalorian warriors from the ''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War]]'' [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series<ref name="TSW6" /> to be the Taung species. "The History of the Mandalorians" further elaborated on the Taungs as the precursors of the Mandalorian culture,<ref name="HotM" /> and the ''[[Galaxy at War]]'' sourcebook provided biological and cultural information on the Taung species.<ref name="GaW" />
